injuries.shortComment: Jennings did not reel in his only target during Sunday's 23-13 win at New Orleans.
injuries.longComment: Jennings again got the second most snaps at wide receiver for the Vikings (47) in Week 5 with Jordan Addison (hamstring) out, but it only translated to one target on the afternoon. Jennings has failed to draw more than two targets in any game so far this season, and his role could be further diminished after Minnesota's bye in Week 6 if Addison is able to return to action.

injuries.shortComment: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and both extra-point tries during the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Reichard got the Vikings on the board early in the first quarter on a 40-yard field goal before connecting on kicks from 54 and 55 yards in the second and fourth quarter, respectively. Reichard has made at least three field goals in each of his last four games and is 15-for-15 on field-goal tries through five games, which is second-best in the NFL behind Spencer Shrader (16-for-16). Reichard is also one of five kickers who have made at least five field goals from 50-plus yards. The Vikings will be on a bye for Week 6 before welcoming in the Colts for Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Murray completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while adding 10 rushes for 51 yards in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
injuries.longComment: Murray completed a season-high 80.0 percent of his passes while patiently carving up the Saints defense Sunday, and the returning Justin Jefferson unsurprisingly accounted for a significant chunk of the quarterback's production through the air with a 6-79-1 line on seven targets. Murray's yardage total was his second-highest of the season as well, trailing only the 247 he generated against the Dolphins in Week 4. The 2019 first overall pick may be starting to hit his stride in head coach Kevin O'Connell's offense, and he'll look to further master the scheme during a Week 6 bye before returning to action in a Week 7 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Jones rushed 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for four yards in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Jones continued handling the workhorse role in Minnesota's backfield, and he finished Sunday's contest with a new season high in carries despite exiting the game for a spell due to a leg issue. Jones added his second rushing touchdown of the season on an eight-yard run early in the fourth quarter, while the 100-yard effort was his second of the campaign. Sunday marked Jones' backfield mate Jordan Mason's fourth absence while on injured reserve due to a thumb injury, and it remains to be seen if the latter will be ready to suit up and put a dent in Jones' opportunities during a Week 7 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Jurgens (elbow) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Jurgens was activated from IR on Saturday. The offensive lineman has recovered from his elbow injury and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Yurosek (ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Yurosek was activated from the Vikings' injured reserve Saturday, just in time for Week 5. The 24-year-old has yet to play in the 2026 season. He is expected to add depth behind T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew versus the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Thorson (hamstring) was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Thorson missed Sunday's Week 4 win over Miami due to his hamstring injury. However, with a pair of full practices to begin Week 5 prep, he's probably good to go for Week 5 versus New Orleans. Thorson should thus reclaim his role as the Vikings' punter.

injuries.shortComment: Cashman recorded eight tackles (three solo) and a fumble recovery during Sunday's 15-10 win versus the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: In a game where Miami's offense simply couldn't stay on the field, Cashman only played 38 defensive snaps. Nevertheless, he managed to rack up seven-plus tackles for his 15th straight contest going back to last season. He's a solid IDP consideration in most formats going into a Week 5 tilt at New Orleans.

injuries.shortComment: Jackson (knee) was placed on injured reserve by the Vikings on Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Jackson suffered a torn meniscus during Sunday's 15-10 win over Miami, and he was already set to miss the rest of the regular season, so Tuesday's move to the IR comes as no surprise. Joe Huber is the top candidate to take over as Minnesota's starting left guard in Jackson's absence.

injuries.shortComment: Claiborne carried the ball three times for 12 yards during Minnesota's win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Claiborne continued to serve a limited role behind Aaron Jones even with Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. Claiborne will look to be more involved offensively during next week's matchup versus the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Metellus recorded nine tackles (four solo), including 0.5 sacks, and a defensed pass Sunday against Tampa Bay in a 23-16 victory.
injuries.longComment: Metellus logged the second-most tackles on Minnesota behind Eric Wilson (11). One of his stops was an assisted sack of Baker Mayfield on the first play of the fourth quarter. Metellus has played every defensive snap for the Vikings so far this season and has racked up 20 tackles and two pass defenses through three contests.

injuries.shortComment: Rodgers logged six tackles (two solo) and an interception in Sunday's 23-16 victory over Tampa Bay.
injuries.longComment: Minnesota led by seven points late in the fourth quarter when Rodgers picked off rookie Jalon Daniels on a last-second heave that drifted just short of the end zone. It was Rodgers' first interception of the season and the fifth of his six-year career. The veteran cornerback emerged as a key starter for Minnesota last season and has played nearly every defensive snap for the team so far in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson finished Sunday's 23-16 victory over Tampa Bay with 10 tackles, including 1.5 sacks, and one defensed pass.
injuries.longComment: Wilson not only led Minnesota with 10 stops, he was also responsible for 1.5 of the team's six total sacks. The veteran linebacker recorded a career-high 6.5 sacks across 17 regular-season games with the Vikings last year, as he's benefitted statistically from being in defensive coordinator Brian Flores' blitz-happy system. Wilson also surpassed 100 tackles for the second time in his career last year and is on pace to do so again in 2026 with 20 stops through three contests.

injuries.shortComment: The Vikings placed Oliver (biceps) on injured reserve Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Oliver's move to IR was expected after the tight end was diagnosed with a torn bicep Monday. The tight end will likely miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season as he recovers from surgery. T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are now the only tight ends on the Vikings' roster, meaning practice-squad elevations ahead of Week 4 will likely include at least one more option at the position. The Vikings signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

injuries.shortComment: Moses (foot) is questionable to play Thursday versus the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Moses was remained limited all week as he nurses a foot injury that he suffered in Week 6 against the Jets, and his status for Week 7 is uncertain as a result. If he is ultimately unable to go, Caleb Lomu would stand to draw the start at right tackle against Chicago on Thursday Night Football.

injuries.shortComment: Canada (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Canada, Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) will all be sidelined for Thursday night's contest, which leaves Christian Gonzalez and Charles Woods as the starters at outside cornerback while Kindle Vildor and Elliott Davison provide depth. It will be the fourth consecutive game that Canada will miss due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Prunty (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Chicago.
injuries.longComment: Prunty will be sidelined for a third-straight game due to a hamstring injury that he picked up during the Patriots' Week 4 win over the Bills. With Carlton Davis (neck) and Channing Canada (hamstring) also ruled out, Charles Woods and Christian Gonzalez will serve as the Patriots' starting outside cornerbacks for Thursday night's game while Elliott Davison and Kindle Vildor provide depth at the position. Prunty's next chance to play is Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Brown injured his knee during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets. He was held out of all three practices during Week 7 prep, and with both Brown and Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) sidelined Thursday, the Patriots will likely turn to Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse to serve as the starting guards against Chicago. Brown will aim to recover enough to return for Week 8 against Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury during the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday. He was unable to practice during the Patriots' short week, and in his absence, Walter Rouse will likely take over as the starting left guard for New England. Vera-Tucker's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.shortComment: Elliss (chest) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Elliss logged three consecutive full practices during Week 7 prep. The linebacker overcame his chest injury in each session and should do the same for Thursday night's game.

injuries.shortComment: Byard (chest) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Byard logged three consecutive full practices during Week 7 prep while dealing with a chest injury. The safety will almost certainly suit up for Thursday's contest and play through what appears to be a minor issue.

injuries.shortComment: Woodson (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Woodson has been dealing with a persistent shoulder injury since Week 4. The strong safety suited up while dealing with the issue in both Week 5 and Week 6, playing 83 percent and 100 percent of the Patriots' defensive snaps in the contests, respectively. Woodson should continue the trend established in previous weeks by suiting up for Thursday's game against the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Davis (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Davis did not participate in Monday's practice but ended the Patriots' short Week 7 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. Despite the upgrade in practice participation, the cornerback is not quite ready to return to the field and will miss his third consecutive game with a neck injury. Charles Woods should once again start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback.

injuries.shortComment: Brown (ankle) does not carry an injury designation going into Thursday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Brown turned in a full practice Wednesday, and that was enough to take him off the injury report going into the Week 7 primetime matchup with Chicago. He returned from a four-game absence in Week 6 and played 76 percent of the offensive snaps against the Jets, recording three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets. Brown and the Patriots will face a Bears defense that allows 9.8 yards per target to opposing receivers.

injuries.shortComment: Bryant (ankle) was a full participant at the Patriots' practice Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Bryant has opened the week with back-to-back full sessions with the Patriots, and he may be trending toward a return to action in the near future. The offensive lineman has missed the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point after picking up an ankle injury during the preseason, but the team opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday. With New England traveling to face the Bears on Thursday, Bryant may not be ready to go in advance of Week 7, but Wednesday's injury report will provide more clarity toward his status.

injuries.shortComment: Borregales made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: All of Borregales' kick attempts came from within 35 yards, with his longest field goal coming from 32 yards. He missed his first extra point of the season, and through six games he has gone 8-for-10 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-15 on extra-point tries. The Patriots will operate on a short practice week ahead of Thursday's road tilt against the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Kiner rushed 11 times for 57 yards while also adding 88 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Kiner stepped into a more prominent role in the backfield behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson in Week 6. With Henderson limited by an ankle injury, Kiner was able to log four more carries than Henderson's seven. Additionally, Kiner averaged 5.2 yards per carry, which was double the 2.6 YPC that Stevenson produced over 14 totes. It's unclear what role Kiner will play when Henderson is back to full health, but he certainly proved he can be productive with an increased workload.

injuries.shortComment: Doubs (shoulder) is hopeful to return after the Patriots' Week 11 bye and isn't expected to face a long-term absence, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: With Doubs already on injured reserve, this report offers a more encouraging timeline after Sunday's shoulder injury. He'll still need to miss at least four games, but a possible return after the bye would keep the Patriots from being without one of their key wide receivers for an extended stretch. Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be in line for increased snaps alongside A.J. Brown and slot man DeMario Douglas with Doubs sidelined.

injuries.shortComment: Henderson (ankle) rushed seven times for 31 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.longComment: Henderson beat the odds by suiting up for Sunday's contest despite what has been reported to be a high-ankle sprain. He was just five yards short of backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson's rushing total despite seeing half the carries, but Henderson's mid-third-quarter fumble did lead to a Jets field goal. Henderson now has a quick turnaround for a Week 7 road matchup against the Bears on Thursday night, so it appears likely he slots into a complementary role again for that contest.

injuries.shortComment: Stevenson rushed 14 times for 36 yards and wasn't targeted in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Stevenson saw twice the rushing workload of backfield mate TreVeyon Henderson but gained only five more yards. Stevenson also recorded 12 of his yards on one carry, so he ran for next to nothing on his other 13 rush attempts in what was his second-least productive game on the ground this season. Henderson did lose a fumble Sunday and is managing what is reportedly a high-ankle sprain, so Stevenson is likely to remain the lead option during a Week 7 road matchup against the Bears on Thursday night.

injuries.shortComment: Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed four times for 24 yards in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Maye got A.J. Brown back from a four-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle injury, but he lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on a 42-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter. That TD was the first of the third-year signal-caller's trio of scoring tosses on the afternoon. Maye connected with DeMario Douglas (nine yards) and Hunter Henry (seven yards) for his other TD strikes, and although he and Brown managed to connect on only three of 10 targets, it was just the second game together for the duo. Maye and the Patriots are right back in action Thursday night for a Week 7 road showdown against the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Henry caught four of five targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Henry's seven-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter proved to be the game-winning score, putting New England ahead 23-16. After not finding the end zone the first four weeks of the season, Henry has scored in back-to-back games. The veteran tight end has been held under 50 yards receiving in five of six contests. He's the definition of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet ahead of Thursday's game with the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas caught seven of eight targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: A.J. Brown returned to the lineup from his ankle injury and led the team with 10 targets, but he dropped multiple passes and finished with a 3-27-0 receiving line. After Romeo Doubs left with a shoulder injury early in the first half following a long touchdown grab, Douglas stepped into an increased offensive role. He ran 26 routes on Drake Maye's 35 dropbacks, and Douglas caught a nine-yard touchdown in the second quarter. He's posted back-to-back big box scores after logging 4-65-2 receiving last Sunday against Las Vegas. The Patriots' slot man doesn't have a big fantasy ceiling but looks like a passable WR4 during bye-week crunches headed into Thursday night's game against the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Campbell (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Campbell sprained his right MCL in the Patriots' Week 5 win over the Raiders. The offensive tackle logged three limited practices during Week 6 prep and will attempt to play through the injury in Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Woods (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Woods aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 5 against the Raiders, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after logging a full practice Friday. He has 22 tackles (16 solo) and three pass defenses through the first five games of the regular season.

injuries.shortComment: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Jones played through a shoulder injury in the Patriots' Week 5 win over the Raiders. The pass rusher logged 57 percent of the Patriots' defensive snaps in the game and will likely have a similar snap share in Week 6 against the Jets.

injuries.shortComment: McKinstry (illness) was a full participant at the Saints' practice Wednesday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: McKinstry left the team's 34-27 win over the Giants in Week 6 with a migraine, but he is now back to full health ahead of Week 7. The 24-year-old will be tasked with trying to slow down DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard in Sunday's matchup with the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Elliss (calf) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Elliss has been sidelined for the Saints' past three games due to a calf injury, but it now seems there's been some progress in his recovery, and he might have a chance to return to game action in Week 7. He'll still probably have to log a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

injuries.shortComment: Shepherd (illness) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
injuries.longComment: Shepherd has missed consecutive games due to an illness. The veteran defensive tackle has returned to practice after recovering from the issue and should be ready to return to the field for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

injuries.shortComment: Donaldson (shoulder) was listed as a limited practice participant Wednesday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: Fellow RB Alvin Kamara (back) also logged a limited session Wednesday, with added context regarding the duo's Week 7 status slated to arrive via Thursday's practice report. In the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants in Week 6, Donaldson recorded six carries for 39 yards and lost a fumble while working alongside Kamara (seven carries for 34 yards and two catches for 35 yards with a TD) as well as Kendre Miller (20 carries for 70 yards).

injuries.shortComment: Kamara (back) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: This now marks three weeks in a row in which Kamara has had practice restrictions due to a back issue, but he's been able to play through it the last two games, accounting for 75 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD on 14 touches during that stretch. The Saints may limit his on-field work Thursday and/or Friday, but there's been no indication he's in danger of missing Sunday's contest against the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Tuesday that Tyson (hamstring) is "getting closer" but won't practice this week, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
injuries.longComment: Tyson made the trip to Paris ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Steelers, but he's not ready to have his 21-day practice window opened just yet. While the Saints haven't provided many specifics regarding where Tyson stands in his recovery from a right hamstring strain beyond noting that he's "improving," the team has a bye coming Week 8, so rookie wideout will be afforded more time to get closer to 100 percent before potentially getting back on the field. If Tyson is able to resume practicing coming out of the bye week, he could be a candidate to make his NFL debut as soon as Nov. 8, when the Saints host the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Werner recorded 11 total tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Werner was able to register double-digit stops for the second straight week and third time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to get to the quarterback in Week 6, sacking Jameis Winston in the second quarter. Through six games so far this year, Werner has compiled 46 total tackles (23 solo), including 2.0 sacks, while also producing two passes defensed.

injuries.shortComment: Emerson recorded seven solo tackles and four passes defensed, including two interceptions, during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Emerson was all over the field in Week 6, finishing second on the team in tackles behind linebacker Pete Werner (11). The cornerback was thrust into a more prominent role in the secondary after Kool-Aid McKinstry was forced out of the game with a migraine, and Emerson definitely didn't disappoint. He was able to reel in a pair of interceptions, picking off Jameis Winston in the third quarter before jumping in front of a pass from J.J. McCarthy one quarter later.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Carlson made two of his three field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Carlson made field goals from 51 and 58 yards while missing a 55-yard kick in the second quarter. Despite the miss, the kicker accounted for 10 of the Saints' 34 points and displayed a strong leg throughout the contest.

injuries.shortComment: Ruiz (knee) made the trip to Paris ahead of the Saints' game against the Steelers in Week 7, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: Ruiz was knocked out of Sunday's game against the Giants early after suffering a knee injury, but it looks like there's still a chance he could be available in Week 7. His activity at practice will be worth keeping an eye on when New Orleans begins preparing for the Paris matchup later in the week.

injuries.shortComment: Vele caught three of six targets for 42 yards during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Vele was on the field for 66 of the Saints' 70 offensive snaps (94.3 percent), which was well ahead of fellow wideouts Chris Olave (42) and rookie Bryce Lance (36). Vele has seen at least six targets in each of the first six games of the regular season, and his 28-294-2 line on 43 targets already surpasses his totals across 13 regular-season games in 2025 (25-293-2 on 40 targets). Given his snap count, it wouldn't be surprising if Vele maintains his role in the offense even if Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) returns, which could come as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25 in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Lance caught two of four passes for nine yards and a touchdown during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Lance's four targets were tied with Alvin Kamara for third most on the Saints behind Chris Olave (seven) and Devaughn Vele (six), with quarterback Tyler Shough completing only 16 of 30 passes. Both of Lance's catches came in the second quarter, the second of which was a two-yard touchdown that tied the game up at 10-10 with five seconds left in the first half. Lance's 36 offensive snaps were third most among New Orleans wide receivers, but his time as the team's WR3 could come to an end as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25, given that rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) is traveling with the team to Paris, per NewOrleans.Football.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Johnson went without a catch in a regular-season contest for the first time since Week 3 of the 2024 campaign. The tight end had reeled in at least three passes in each of the team's first five games of the year. Over the last two weeks, Johnson has caught four of seven targets for 16 yards, and his next chance to get back on track will come in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Miller carried the ball 20 times for 70 yards and caught both his targets for zero yards in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Alvin Kamara missed time in the first half due to an undisclosed injury, and while he was able to return and make an impact as a pass catcher, Miller led the Saints in rushing yards and touches with 22. The 70 yards also represented his best total since Week 18 of his rookie season in 2023. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) not eligible to return until after a Week 8 bye, Miller should split reps in the backfield with Kamara once again in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Shough completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants. He added 32 yards and a TD on five carries.
injuries.longComment: While he didn't produce much yardage, Shough kept the Saints' offense humming, connecting with Bryce Lance, Alvin Kamara and Chris Olave for scores through the air while adding a one-yard touchdown on the ground in the third quarter. Shough has been playing through a couple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which could help explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks, but the second-year QB showed he can be plenty productive despite the injury. Shough will take a 12:5 TD:INT through six games into a Week 7 tilt against the Steelers in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Olave caught four of seven targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: While he didn't see his usual volume on an afternoon in which Tyler Shough threw for only 144 yards, Olave was on the other end of one of the QB's three scores, hauling in an 18-yard TD early in the fourth quarter that proved to be crucial after the Giants staged a late, but unsuccessful, rally. Olave got double-digit targets in each of the first four games of the season, but over the last two contests he's been targeted just 13 times, posting an 8-89-1 line. He'll look to regain some steam in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Steelers.

injuries.shortComment: Riley sustained a neck injury in the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
injuries.longComment: Riley suffered a neck injury late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. Coach Kellen Moore seemed confident the cornerback is okay, but Week 7 preparation should offer more insight on the injury.

injuries.shortComment: Wood (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Wood missed the Saints' last four games while on injured reserve due to a calf strain. He's been cleared to return Sunday and will resume his duties as the team's long snapper.

injuries.shortComment: Wright (concussion) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
injuries.longComment: The rookie fourth-rounder was unavailable for the Saints' Week 5 loss to the Vikings while in the league's concussion protocol. Wright has been cleared from protocol by an independent neurologist, and his return gives the Saints more depth on the offensive line.

injuries.shortComment: Broughton (illness) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants, Jeff Nowak of The Big 870 New Orleans reports.
injuries.longComment: Broughton was a full practice participant Friday, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He has six tackles (one solo), one forced fumble and a fumble recovery across four regular-season games.

injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Newsome (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Newsome was knocked out of Sunday's game versus the Saints early by a concussion, and now his availability for Week 7 is in jeopardy. He'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before getting the green light to return to full-contact football activities, and whether he's able to return to practice Thursday or Friday may shed some light on any potential progress.

injuries.shortComment: Holland (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Holland presumably suffered the concussion during Sunday's game versus the Saints, and now his status for Week 7 is up in the air. He'll need to clear league concussion protocol before being allowed to return to game action, and his activity at practice Thursday and Friday could offer some insight into any progress he makes as the week continues.

injuries.shortComment: Edmunds (shoulder) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Edmunds hurt his shoulder on the final play of Sunday's game versus the Saints, and now his availability for Week 7 is in question. Any chance he has of suiting up at Houston will likely hinge on whether he's able to get back on the practice field Thursday or Friday.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson (neck) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Johnson was practicing in a limited capacity in the leadup to the Giants' matchup versus the Saints in Week 6, but he ultimately downgraded to missing practice later in the week before sitting out that contest. He'll likely have to participate fully in practice Thursday or Friday to dodge taking an injury designation into the weekend.

injuries.shortComment: The Giants designated Adebo (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Adebo was placed on the Giants' injured reserve following the team's Week 1 win over the Cowboys due to a knee injury. He's been sidelined for the last five games, but he's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session, per Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site. Adebo would need to be activated from IR by Saturday at 4:00 p.m. ET in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Mooney (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Mooney wasn't cleared to return to this past Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints after injuring his neck in the fourth quarter, but he evidently responded well to treatment and faced no restrictions as the Giants returned to the field to begin Week 7 prep. With Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely demanding most of the looks in the passing game this season, Mooney has struggled to carve out consistent weekly volume. Through six appearances, Mooney has been targeted 19 times and has recorded an 8-109-0 receiving line while also adding 29 yards on two carries.

injuries.shortComment: McCarthy will start at quarterback in Week 7, coach John Harbaugh confirmed Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Things had been trending in this direction after McCarthy's impressive performance in relief of Jameis Winston in Week 6. Giants coach John Harbaugh made it official Wednesday afternoon as the team looks to see what it has in the recently acquired McCarthy. He completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards with a touchdown and a pick in limited action against the Saints and had a pair of 40-yard completions.

injuries.shortComment: Winston is in line to serve as the Giants' backup quarterback Sunday against the Texans with the team planning to move forward with J.J. McCarthy as its starter in Week 7, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: After Jaxson Dart (knee) went down with a likely season-ending injury in a Week 2 loss to the Rams, Winston stepped in as the starter for the subsequent four games. Though Winston led the Giants to a respectable 2-1-1 record while completing 60.3 percent of his passes for 6.5 yards per attempt and a 7:4 TD:INT during that stretch, he had a rough showing in this past Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints before being pulled early in the fourth quarter. McCarthy proceeded to take over under center and nearly guided the Giants all the way back from a 24-point deficit, so he'll be rewarded with the starting nod for at least Week 7. Given that the 23-year-old McCarthy is a recent first-round pick who could have a longer-term future in New York or represent an appealing trade chip down the road, it wouldn't be surprising if he was given a long leash as the team's starter.

injuries.shortComment: Reese logged six tackles (four solo) and a fumble recovery during the Giants' loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Reese had another solid outing despite the loss, as he managed to recover the first fumble of his career. The 21-year-old has gotten off to a strong start in his rookie season, racking up 49 tackles (34 solo), including 1.0 sacks, an interception and a fumble recovery across his first six games.

injuries.shortComment: Zvada made both of his field-goal attempts and his sole PAT in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Zvada had a strong Week 6 bounceback after going 2-for-5 on field-goal attempts in Week 5. The kicker made 30-yard and 41-yard field goals in the loss, so he still may struggle with distance and consistency as the season continues.

injuries.shortComment: Fields caught two of eight targets for 19 yards during the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Fields' eight targets were a career high for the rookie third-rounder and third most among Giants pass catchers behind Malik Nabers (15) and Isaiah Likely (11). However, Fields had only two receptions to show for it, and he's logged two catches in each of the first six games of his NFL career. The Giants will hit the road for Week 7 against the Texans, and Fields could be working with J.J. McCarthy rather than Jameis Winston for that contest.

injuries.shortComment: Singletary turned four carries into 14 yards and hauled in his lone target for 19 yards during Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Singletary was back in action Sunday after being a healthy scratch in each of the Giants' three games prior to Week 6. Three of his four carries went for two yards or fewer, although he did log a nine-yard rush and 19-yard catch on back-to-back plays early in the fourth quarter. Singletary's 31 offensive snaps were most among Giants running backs, but the team's backfield situation is a mess, given Cam Skattebo saw the field for only six offensive snaps and did not record a carry. The Giants will hit the road for Week 7 against the Texans on Oct. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Likely caught six of 11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints.
injuries.longComment: The tight end came through with another big performance and connected with J.J. McCarthy on a 24-yard TD in the fourth quarter after the young QB had replaced Jameis Winston under center. It's reassuring that Likely remained involved even after the switch at quarterback, and he's seen double-digit targets in three straight games, delivering a 24-259-3 line on 36 targets as the team's No. 2 pass catcher behind Malik Nabers. Likely will look to keep rolling in Week 7 against the Texans, regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

injuries.shortComment: Skattebo played only six snaps and got zero carries or targets in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: One week after losing a key fumble in a 27-27 tie to the Commanders, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown but managing just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches, while Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. With no one really stepping up in his place, Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back in fantasy lineups until one emerges from the pack.

injuries.shortComment: Nabers caught 12 of 15 targets for 165 yards in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints.
injuries.longComment: Jameis Winston got benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter after throwing his second interception of the day, but Nabers stayed busy no matter who was under center for the Giants, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. The third-year wideout topped 100 yards for a third straight game, a stretch in which he's racked up a 29-398-2 line on 42 targets, but a potential full-time switch to McCarthy under center will create a little extra uncertainty for Nabers heading into a Week 7 tilt against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Mauigoa (thigh) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Mauigoa is considered week-to-week with a thigh injury. The linebacker exited the Jets' Week 6 loss to the Patriots early due to the injury and did not return to the contest.

injuries.shortComment: Parham (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Wednesday was Parham's first practice since sustaining a knee injury in Week 3 against the Lions, which prevented him from playing in each of the Jets' three following games. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If Parham is cleared to return, then he would likely reclaim his starting job at left guard from Jordan Meredith.

injuries.shortComment: Nwangwu (knee) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Nwangwu likely picked up his back issue during the six special-teams snaps he played in the Jets' Week 6 loss to the Patriots. It remains unclear how significant the running back's injury is and whether he will be able to suit up for Week 7 against the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Ossai (ankle) was listed as a DNP on Wednesday's practice report.
injuries.longComment: Ossai was unable to play against the Patriots in Week 6, and Rich Cimini of ESPN.com notes that the veteran defensive end is still considered week-to-week due to an ankle injury. If Ossai is not cleared to return for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins, then Will McDonald (toe) and Nate Lynn would be the Jets' depth options at defensive end behind Kingsley Enagbare and 2026 second-overall pick David Bailey.

injuries.shortComment: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Hall (quadriceps) won't practice Wednesday but hasn't been ruled out from playing Sunday versus the Dolphins, Al Iannazzone of Newsday reports.
injuries.longComment: At the beginning of each of the previous three weeks, Glenn had classified Hall as being "week-to-week" in his recovery from a right quad issue, but the coach didn't apply that same label to the running back to begin Week 7 prep. Though Hall isn't yet ready to practice after missing the Jets' previous three games, he could be able to get back on the field in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday, which would leave the door open for him to suit up Sunday. Whenever Hall returns, he'll reclaim starting duties out of the backfield, though Glenn acknowledged that Braelon Allen is "going to get touches, too" after impressing while filling in for Hall over the past three contests, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.

injuries.shortComment: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Mitchell (finger) will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Mitchell will take part in practice for the first time since Week 3, after missing the Jets' last four games due to an injury to a finger on his right hand that he ultimately needed surgery to address. While the wideout's return to practice in any fashion is an encouraging sign, he may need to turn in a full session by Friday in order for the Jets to feel confident in his chances of suiting up Sunday versus the Dolphins. If Mitchell winds up missing a fifth consecutive game, rookie first-round pick Omar Cooper would likely continue to enjoy an expanded profile in the New York passing game behind top target Garrett Wilson.

injuries.shortComment: Sherwood recorded 11 tackles (six solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery during Sunday's 26-19 loss at New England.
injuries.longComment: Sherwood made a huge hustle play on a third down early in the fourth quarter, punching the ball out of the arms of DeMario Douglas after chasing him down 39 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. He also recovered a fumble in the third quarter, and both turnovers set up Jets field goals. He profiles as a solid IDP option in many formats heading into a Week 7 tilt versus the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Belton recorded nine tackles (four solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 26-19 loss at New England.
injuries.longComment: In a game where the Patriots were able to keep the ball on the ground for much of the day, Belton collected six-plus tackles for his fifth straight contest. He's on pace for a career year in that category, and he projects as a solid IDP option in many formats going into a Week 7 matchup versus the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Davis rushed seven times for 16 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards during Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Davis was on the field for just eight offensive snaps, but the running back had a touch on each of those snaps. He entered Week 6 having toted the rock just two times over five contests, so his increase in workload was a positive turn of events. With Breece Hall (quadriceps) still uncertain for Week 7, Davis could operate as the primary backup behind Braelon Allen again versus the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Patrick caught one of three targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Patrick was unable to have much of an impact in Week 6, finishing tied for fourth on the team in targets with tight end Kenyon Sadiq. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) still banged up, Patrick could get another crack at operating in a prominent role in New York's offense in Week 7 versus Miami.

injuries.shortComment: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts and his sole PAT in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Sanders had a stellar game, contributing 13 of the Jets' 19 total points in the contest. The kicker made field goals from 42, 36, 40 and 36 yards in the contest, keeping the Jets in the game until the very end.

injuries.shortComment: Taylor caught four of six targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Taylor put together his best performance of the year, setting new season highs in catches, yards and targets. The tight end now has caught nine of 12 targets for 55 yards over four games this season. With rookie Kenyon Sadiq also heavily involved at tight end, Taylor's upside will continue to be hard to gauge moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Cooper brought in six of seven targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Making his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle sprain suffered on the opening possession of the season, Cooper hit the ground running and finished as the team leader in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The Indiana product also recorded his first NFL touchdown on a 48-yard strike from Geno Smith early in the third quarter, and his instant production despite the layoff gives his fantasy outlook a significant boost heading into a Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins.

injuries.shortComment: Smith completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding two rushes for minus-1 yard in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Smith took three sacks while trying to play catch-up all afternoon, and in that context, his final numbers were all the more impressive. The veteran signal-caller helped the Jets claw back from a 17-3 halftime deficit to get within four entering the fourth quarter, but his interception at the Patriots' 24-yard line early in the period snuffed out a potential scoring opportunity. Smith has certainly given New York some much-needed veteran stability at the quarterback position and displayed encouraging chemistry with returning rookie Omar Cooper (6-103-1) on Sunday, so there's reason for optimism heading into a favorable Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Allen rushed 17 times for 78 yards and brought in both targets for 26 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Allen served as the Jets' clear lead back during Breece Hall's second straight absence due to a quadriceps injury, and the former put together a productive effort that featured a new season high in receiving yards. Allen has acquitted himself very well as the No. 1 option over the last two games, posting 194 rushing yards and a touchdown alongside three receptions and the 26 receiving yards he accrued Sunday. If Hall remains sidelined in Week 7, Allen will get a crack at a beatable Dolphins defense at home.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson brought in four of six targets for 44 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Wilson had an early catch and then had a quiet middle portion of the game before rounding out his line some in the fourth quarter. Wilson still finished with modest production overall, as his reception and receiving yards totals were both his second lowest of the campaign. Geno Smith has undergone his fair share of struggles in his return to New York this season, but Wilson remains his top target with 48 looks from the veteran signal-caller over the first six games. Wilson will take a 35-418-3 line into a Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Sadiq caught one of three targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Sadiq was able to clear concussion protocol during the week, but the rookie tight end has been playing through minor injuries all season. Since catching seven passes for 105 yards in Week 3 against the Lions, Sadiq has just three catches for 15 yards on 10 targets over the last three contests. He's become waiver-wire fodder in redraft leagues.

injuries.shortComment: Williams should continue to serve as the No. 3 wide receiver behind Garrett Wilson and Tim Patrick for Sunday's game against the Patriots due to the absence of Adonai Mitchell (finger).
injuries.longComment: Williams caught one of his two targets for 16 yards and rushed once for three yards in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns. The wide receiver should continue to see some attention from Geno Smith, but if Omar Cooper (ankle) is activated from IR for Sunday's game, that could change.

injuries.shortComment: Bailey recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 3.0 sacks, during the Jets' 17-12 win over the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The Browns' offensive line had trouble containing Bailey and the Jets' pass rush Sunday, with New York sacking Deshaun Watson eight times. Three of those sacks were credited to Bailey, two of which were on third down and forced the Browns to punt on the next play. The Week 5 effort was the performance that the Jets were hoping to see out of the second overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. Bailey is up to 5.0 sacks through five regular-season games, which leads the Jets and is tied with D.J. Wonnum for fourth most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (7.5), Greg Rousseau (6.0) and Dallas Turner (5.5).

injuries.shortComment: Enagbare (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuries.longComment: Enagbare ended Week 5 prep with a full practice after logging consecutive sessions with a knee injury to start the week. The defensive end is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest as a starting pass rusher for the Jets' defense.

injuries.shortComment: DeJean posted five solo tackles and a pass defense in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers in Week 6.
injuries.longComment: DeJean has logged at least five tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and has played every defensive snap in four of those contests. He's up to 39 tackles (23 solo) and five pass defenses (including one interception) on the season, and he's fourth on the Eagles in combined takcles behind Jihaad Campbell (47) and Zack Baun (42).

injuries.shortComment: Baun registered six tackles (four solo) and a pass defense during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers in Week 6.
injuries.longComment: Baun was one of three Eagles players to play all 79 defensive snaps, and his six combined tackles were tied for third-most on the team behind Arnold Ebiketie (nine) and Andrew Mukuba (eight). Through five regular-season games, Baun has accumulated 42 tackles (22 solo) and four pass defenses, and he is on track to crack 100-plus tackles for a third consecutive year.

injuries.shortComment: Cooper caught one of two targets for nine yards and added 38 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Cooper saw his offensive workload decrease with the return of DeVonta Smith in Week 6, and, as a result, this was the first time he's failed to reel in multiple passes since Week 3. With Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon all active, Cooper's ceiling will be limited from a fantasy perspective moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports that teams seeking help at wide receiver will likely call the Eagles about the status of Brown before the Nov. 10 deadline.
injuries.longComment: Brown's lone regular-season game this season was in Week 2 against the Titans, when he rushed for 12 yards on two carries and did not record a target. He missed the next three games due to an ankle injury and was a healthy scratch for Week 6 against the Panthers, and the veteran wide receiver doesn't appear to be in the Eagles' offensive gameplan moving forward. The Eagles have a 2-4 record, and with franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts (calf) likely out for the rest of the season, the team could be looking to trade Brown and other players by the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

injuries.shortComment: Elliott made both of his extra-point attempts during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: With Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the year, Sunday was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center. The offense labored to get up and down the field, and it was the fifth time in six games that Elliott attempted zero or one field goals. Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26 could be a better night offensively for the Eagles, given that Dallas' defense ranks 30th in the league in yards allowed per game.

injuries.shortComment: Wicks caught two of four passes for 24 yards during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Wicks' 24 receiving yards were his second lowest of the season, but he still finished third among Eagles pass catchers in that category Sunday behind DeVonta Smith (75) and Dallas Goedert (61). Week 6 was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center, and with Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the rest of the season, the scoring floors of Wicks and the other Philadelphia pass catchers figure to be lower moving forward. That said, the Eagles have a juicy Week 7 matchup on Monday, Oct. 26 against the Cowboys, whose defense ranks in the bottom-10 in the league in fantasy points allowed per game to wide receivers.

injuries.shortComment: Hurts (calf) is expected to be held out of football activities for multiple months and miss the rest of the season after new imaging over the weekend revealed several blood clots in his lungs, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injuries.longComment: Initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot after being cleated in the left calf in an Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, Hurts had been cleared by doctors to play in Week 5 in the Eagles' loss to the Jaguars in London before more recent testing last week showed that the blood clot had moved. According to a statement released Monday by his agent, Nicole Lynn, Hurts now has been diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis in the left calf, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. Hurts has gone on blood thinners to treat the blood clots, and while his prognosis is good and he's not expected to face any long-term health effects, he won't be able to participate in football activities until he's off blood thinners. With that in mind, Hurts isn't expected to make a push for a late-season return from injured reserve and instead will turn his focus toward returning to full health in 2027. The Eagles will move forward with Tanner McKee, Cole Payton and Joe Milton as their options at quarterback.

injuries.shortComment: McKee completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while adding one carry for no gain in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
injuries.longComment: McKee's completion total was impressive, but he averaged a modest 4.8 yards per attempt on the afternoon despite having DeVonta Smith back from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. McKee's longest completion of the day went for 19 yards to Smith on a fourth-quarter scoring strike, which brought Philadelphia to within five at the time. McKee ultimately wasn't able to complete the comeback in the first installment of what figures to be an extended starting assignment in place of Jalen Hurts (IR, calf), and he'll look to be more aggressive during a Week 7 home divisional clash with the Cowboys next Monday night.

injuries.shortComment: Pierce rushed 12 times for 35 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 15 yards in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Pierce handled all the running back carries for the Eagles with all of Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Tank Bigsby (IR, abdomen) and Will Shipley (IR, foot) unavailable. As his rushing line suggests, Pierce found running room mostly at a premium, but he managed his first touchdown on the ground since the 2024 season on a two-yard run late in the first half. Pierce also was surprisingly involved as a receiver with Tanner McKee quarterbacking the offense, and the veteran back will remain in a similar role in a Week 7 home matchup against the Cowboys next Monday night if Barkley remains out.

injuries.shortComment: Smith brought in seven of 14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Smith had an eventful day in his return from a two-game absence, leading the Eagles in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon. He also worked around getting briefly shaken up following a long incompletion where he appeared to have taken a blow to the chest area, and he added his second touchdown reception of the campaign via a 19-yard grab early in the fourth quarter. Smith displayed solid chemistry with fill-in signal-caller Tanner McKee, which certainly is a welcome development considering Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) is sidelined indefinitely.

injuries.shortComment: Lemon caught three of six targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout briefly exited Week 6 with an undisclosed injury but quickly returned and ended up running a team-high 45 routes on Tanner McKee's 49 dropbcks. It still didn't result in much production, as Lemon's six targets were a distant third on the team. The first-round wide receiver has just 18 catches for 127 yards and no touchdowns on 28 targets through six games. He can't be trusted as a fantasy starter headed into next Monday night's game against the Cowboys.

injuries.shortComment: Goedert caught six of eight targets for 61 yards during Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Goedert was able to reel in exactly six passes for the second straight week while his eight targets were second only to DeVonta Smith (14). With Jalen Hurts (calf) on injured reserve with a superficial blood clot, Tanner McKee took over at starting quarterback Sunday, logging 45 pass attempts in the defeat. If Philadelphia remains pass-heavy moving forward, Goedert will stand to continue seeing plenty of looks.

injuries.shortComment: Smith (concussion) won't return to Sunday's game against Carolina.
injuries.longComment: Smith took a hit from Chuba Hubbard in the second quarter. He exited for an evaluation in the medical tent and was then escorted to the locker room by the training staff. With Smith ruled out for the remainder of Week 6, the Eagles will need to rely on Jonathan Greenard, Arnold Ebiketie and Keyshawn James-Newby to fill the void.

injuries.shortComment: Kendall (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Kendall ended the week with consecutive limited practices. The center has recovered from his knee injury in time to suit up for Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Payton is active as the backup to starting quarterback Tanner McKee in Sunday's game against the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: A rookie fifth-round pick out of North Dakota State, Payton has yet to make his NFL debut, but he's one step closer to doing so after Jalen Hurts (calf) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. Payton had slotted third or fourth on the depth chart through the first five games of the season, but he'll be dressing as the No. 2 option Sunday while McKee draws his third career NFL start. Since he's set to become a free agent after the season and may not be viewed as the Eagles' long-term plan at the backup quarterback spot, McKee could be in danger of losing his grip on the starting job if he struggles in his extended snaps while Hurts remains out indefinitely. Payton could be someone to keep an eye on if the Eagles decide to give him a look at any point, as he displayed intriguing rushing skills during his collegiate career and gained 45 yards on three carries during his limited preseason action.

injuries.shortComment: Bennett (knee) won't come off injured reserve this weekend and has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 6 battle against Carolina.
injuries.longComment: Bennett hasn't yet played this season after hurting his knee during training camp. However, he had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday and upgraded to full practice participation Friday following a pair of limited sessions, so the third-year cornerback could make his season debut next Monday against Dallas.

injuries.shortComment: Dickerson (knee) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Dickerson remains on injured reserve after he wasn't activated Saturday despite having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the week. Willie Lampkin should make another start at left guard for the Eagles.

injuries.shortComment: The Eagles have downgraded Stowers (quadriceps) to out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Stowers will have to wait at least another week before making his regular-season NFL debut after he had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week. Stowers should see snaps as a catch-first tight end behind Dallas Goedert once he's ready to return to game action.

injuries.shortComment: The Eagles downgraded Calcaterra (back) to out Saturday for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Calcaterra remains on injured reserve, though his 21-day practice window was opened earlier in the week. He's nearing a return, though his role is unclear behind Dallas Goedert and potentially even block-first TE Johnny Mundt.

injuries.shortComment: Elliott (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: It's the first time Elliott has logged a full practice since his 21-day window to return from injured reserve opened Oct. 8. The Steelers released Rayshawn Jenkins earlier Wednesday, and that's a potential sign that Elliott will be available to make his 2026 debut this Sunday against the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Skowronek (calf) did not practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Skowronek was unable to play against the Buccaneers in Week 6 due to a calf injury that he sustained during the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Colts. He'll have two more chances to log at least a limited practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Dowdle was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Dowdle had missed three consecutive games due to a dislocated toe on his right foot before returning to action for this past Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers. While playing 21 of the Steelers' 79 offensive snaps, Dowdle finished with seven carries for 40 yards and added three catches for nine yards, but he appears to have emerged from the contest with a new injury. His ability to practice in any capacity to begin Week 7 is generally a good sign, but Dowdle may need to upgrade to full participation by Friday to avoid carrying a designation into Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Brisker posted seven tackles (four solo) during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Brisker played every single defensive snap for the fifth time in six games this season, and he has logged at least six tackles in each of those outings. He's up to 41 combined tackles in 2026 and is on track to crack 100 tackles for the third time in his NFL career and the first time since 2023, when he played for the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson recorded 11 tackles (seven solo) during Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: Payton led the Steelers in tackles Sunday, and it was the third time he's logged double-digit stops this season. The third-year linebacker is up to 55 combined tackles, which leads the Steelers and is eighth-most in the NFL. He should remain busy in Week 7 against the Saints, whose offense, led by QB Tyler Shough, put up 34 points in a win over the Giants in Week 6.

injuries.shortComment: Herbig recorded six solo tackles, including 2.0 sacks, during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Herbig did not record a sack through the first five games of the regular season, but the fourth-year pro got to quarterback Jalon Daniels twice during Sunday's OT victory. Herbig is up to 18 tackles (13 solo) and one forced fumble through six regular-season games while working in a rotational role on defense.

injuries.shortComment: Ramsey tallied 10 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Ramsey was responsible for two of the Steelers' five sacks on Jalon Daniels during Sunday's OT win. Ramsey's first sack came on the third play of the game, and his second sack on Daniels was on a fourth-and-8 in overtime to seal the game for the Steelers. Ramsey has accumulated 19 total tackles over his last two games and is up to 37 stops (23 solo), two pass defenses and one forced fumble through six regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Boswell went 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts while making both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 26-19 overtime win against Tampa Bay.
injuries.longComment: Boswell converted multiple field goals for the second week in a row and the fourth time overall in 2026. The kicker pulled his first field-goal attempt of the day wide left from 48 yards out in the first quarter, but he responded by adding makes from 52, 39 and 20 yards before the end of regulation. Boswell now has gone 13-for-17 on field-goal tries, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, while making all 12 of his PATs over the team's first six contests this year.

injuries.shortComment: Freiermuth caught two of three targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Bucs.
injuries.longComment: Freiermuth entered Week 6 questionable due to a calf injury, but he ended up running 41 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 56 dropbacks. The tight end just didn't do much in the box score and was targeted on just 6.1 percent of Rodgers' 49 pass attempts. Freiermuth has already scored four touchdowns this season but has just 180 receiving yards on 21 grabs across 29 targets through six games. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option.

injuries.shortComment: Metcalf caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: The targets and catches were season highs for Metcalf, while the veteran WR came up just short of his second 100-yard performance in the last three weeks. Metcalf will take a 30-318-1 line on 52 targets into a Week 7 clash with the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Warren carried the ball 14 times for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: While Warren still led the Steelers' backfield, his touch volume and production took a dip as Rico Dowdle returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury, with Dowdle turning 10 touches into 49 scrimmage yards. As long as coach Mike McCarthy insists on using a timeshare between the two, Warren will be hard-pressed to repeat the outstanding numbers he compiled while Dowdle was on the shelf. Warren will try to make a bigger impact in Week 7 against the Saints in Paris.

injuries.shortComment: Rodgers completed 33 of 49 passes for 253 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: Down 16-3 to begin the fourth quarter, Rodgers began the comeback with a five-yard TD pass to Darnell Washington before leading the Steelers on three straight field-goal drives. The veteran QB then put together a 12-play, 70-yard drive to begin OT that was capped with a six-yard score to Germie Bernard. Rodgers has tossed multiple touchdowns in four straight games, posting an 11:4 TD:INT over that stretch and giving him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 7 trip to Paris to face the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Washington caught four of six targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Bucs.
injuries.longComment: The Steelers entered the fourth quarter trailing 16-3, but Washington sparked the comeback with a five-yard touchdown to make it 16-10. It was the big tight end's second touchdown of the season, and he's now recorded 15 grabs for 156 yards and the two scores on 22 targets through six games. He's on pace for a career year in the receiving department and is a preferred target of Aaron Rodgers near the goal line due to his sheer size advantage.

injuries.shortComment: Bernard caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Bucs.
injuries.longComment: With Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) out for the Steelers, Bernard was the clear WR2 behind DK Metcalf and actually ran a team-high 54 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 56 dropbacks. Metcalf edged Bernard out in targets 15 to 12, while both players caught 11 passes. Pittman and Wilson are both required to miss at least two and three more games, respectively, so Bernard is locked into an every-down role for the immediate future. Rodgers has sung the rookie wideout's praises early this season, and it's reasonable to expect Bernard to remain a key part of the passing offense moving forward. He should be rostered in all fantasy formats.

injuries.shortComment: Echols (hamstring) won't return to Sunday's game against Tampa Bay, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Echols was injured on a Buccaneers punt in the first half. He limped off the field and was eventually ruled out coming out of halftime due to a hamstring injury. With Echols done for the remainder of Week 6, rookie Daylen Everette will need to step up.

injuries.shortComment: Dean (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
injuries.longComment: Dean was a limited participant throughout Week 6 prep. The cornerback is all set to suit up in Sunday's contest, likely playing through the remains of his ankle injury.

injuries.shortComment: Dugger (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Dugger appears to have picked up a knee injury in the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Commanders. The strongside linebacker's ability to practice in the first Week 7 prep session is a strong sign that he should be able to suit up for Sunday's contest against the Falcons. Dugger will likely need to upgrade to full participation by Friday's session to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Williams (knee) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Williams likely sustained his knee injury in the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Commanders on Monday night. It is unclear how significant the defensive end's issue is. Still, he will need to achieve some level of practice participation by Friday to have any hope of suiting up for Sunday's game against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Sigle (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Sigle has not practiced since being diagnosed as week-to-week with the high-ankle sprain he sustained in the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. Wednesday's injury report signals that Malik Mustapha is once again taking first-team reps at strong safety in Sigle's place in anticipation of the team's Week 7 game against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Bosa (calf) Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Bosa remains sidelined with a calf injury he suffered during the 49ers' Week 2 win over the Dolphins. Coach Kyle Shanahan hopes Bosa will practice Thursday, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports. Shanahan's statement makes it seem like Bosa has an outside chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Falcons. If the defensive end cannot, he will have to wait until after the 49ers' Week 8 bye to return to the field.

injuries.shortComment: Kirk (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: It's the first time that Kirk has logged a full session since his 21-day practice window opened Thursday. He was not activated from IR before this past Monday's game against the Commanders, but it looks like the veteran wide receiver is trending in the right direction ahead of Sunday's road game against the Falcons. Kirk's availability is sorely needed for a 49ers wideout group that will be without Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and could also be without Mike Evans (ribs), the latter of whom aggravated a right Achilles injury during the first half of Monday's win.

injuries.shortComment: Evans (ribs/Achilles) officially didn't practice Wednesday, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: As expected, Evans didn't mix into drills just two days removed from exiting Monday's game against the Commanders early due to an Achilles injury. Afterward, coach Kyle Shanahan termed the issue right Achilles soreness, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com, which isn't believed to be a long-term concern. Shanahan also expressed hope that Evans will be able to play Sunday in Atlanta, but in the end the 49ers likely will exercise caution with the top wide receiver on the roster.

injuries.shortComment: Samuel (hamstring) is not expected to practice Wednesday, Cam Inman of Bay Area News Group reports.
injuries.longComment: The 49ers are coming off a Monday Night Football win and therefore not holding an official practice Wednesday. That being said, coach Kyle Shanahan said that Samuel would not be practicing. Samuel is working his way back from his hamstring injury and the sense is that a return after the 49ers' Week 8 bye is more realistic at this stage.

injuries.shortComment: Warner totaled eight tackles (six solo) during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Warner was on the field for every single defensive snap for a fourth consecutive game, and he finished second on the 49ers in tackles behind Jaden Dugger (11). Warner has logged at least seven tackles in five of six regular-season games, and his 58 combined tackles are third-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (68) and Ernest Jones (59). The 49ers will hit the road for Week 7 against the Falcons on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Pineiro made his lone field-goal attempt and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Pineiro's extra-point try late in the first quarter missed wide to the right, but he connected on a 33-yard field goal late in the third quarter to give the 49ers a 23-3 lead. Through six regular-season games, the veteran kicker has gone 6-for-9 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-22 on extra-point tries. He hasn't been the most accurate kicker, but Pineiro's scoring floor will remain elevated with a 49ers team that ranks third in the NFL in points per game (29.5) and ninth in yards per game (366.7).

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout's removal from Monday's 23-17 win over the Commanders was due to an AC sprain in his shoulder, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Stout's practice reps during Week 6 prep were limited due to his shoulder injury. He was cleared to play Monday but was hampered by his injury, which led to Stout being replaced by Ashtyn Davis in the second half and finishing with two tackles over a season-low 25 snaps. Stout's practice participation over the coming days will provide some clarity on his status for Sunday's road game against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Greenlaw was reinstated by the NFL on Tuesday after he served a one-game suspension in Week 6, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Greenlaw was back at practice Tuesday after missing the team's 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday Night Football. The 29-year-old will return to his starting role at weakside linebacker in Week 7 against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Watkins caught his lone target for 22 yards during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Watkins connected with Brock Purdy for a big gain early in the second quarter, and all three of wideout's catches this season have gone for 20-plus yards. Watkins' 47 offensive snaps ended up leading all 49ers wide receivers, and the second-year pro's role in the passing game could expand in Week 7 against the Falcons, depending on the availability of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring).

injuries.shortComment: Cowing accrued zero targets during Monday's 23-17 win against Washington.
injuries.longComment: Despite the absence of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the premature exit of Mike Evans (Achilles), Cowing went without a catch for the fifth time this season. With neither Samuel nor Evans a lock to suit up in Week 7 versus the Falcons, Cowing might see more snaps alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. However, that may not be the case if Demarcus Robinson (ankle) can manage to get on the field after spending time on injured reserve since the Week 2 win over Miami.
